independentAnswers.basis: Standard hyperbola is centered at the origin.
Focus/directrix give x²=8y; substituting (-4,a) yields 16=8a.
Only x²−4y²−2x+16y−11=0 has opposite-sign quadratic terms; the other four complete to real ellipses.
For y²=8x, tangent slope −2 has y-intercept p/m=−1; its x-intercept is −1/2.
Vertical transverse axis has a=3,c=5,b=4, so y²/9−x²/16=1, equivalent to choice ⑤.
AF+FB=AB=10 and parabola distances equal perpendicular distances to l; trapezoid area is (10/2)·HH'=30.

As supplied, 3x²+4y²=120 gives x²/40+y²/30=1. Choices ① (foci ±(1,0)), ② (distance sum 30), ④ (axes 4 and 2√3), and ⑤ (tangent intercept ±√7) are all false; the single-choice item has no unique answer.
A tangent from (0,3) to x²−y²=12 touches at y=−4, x=±2√7; slopes are ±√7/2, with listed negative slope in ⑤.
For P on the diameter circle, PF²+PF'²=28; hyperbola gives |PF−PF'|=4, hence PF·PF'=6.
A chord through focus F has variable direction. For fixed ellipse foci ±4, area of ABF' varies with direction; area 20 alone does not determine a,b or a+b. Diagram adds no stated restriction.
y²=x/2 has p=1/8. For P=(8,2), AP=10 and PF=65/8; the derivative of AP+PF along the parabola vanishes there and it is the minimum.

Shared foci plus the supplied ellipse x²/36+y²/11=10 give c²=250 and hyperbola a²=241. Their intersection yields x²=241·36/25, so |PF²−PF'²|−a² is not any listed integer choice; the supplied item is inconsistent with its choices.
Parallelogram area F'QFP is 12b=24, so b=2; hyperbola then gives a=5 in quadrant I.
Intersection in quadrant II is P=(−5/9,4√5/3); PQ=49/9 and PR=41/9, sum 10.
For y²=8x, focus distances 10 and 4 give A=(8,8), B=(2,−4); area OAB is 24.
Midpoint y=3/2 gives m²=1/4; chord length is 4(1+m²)=5.
Tangent is 8x−y=15; intersections with y=±2x average to centroid (4/3,2/3).
Nonzero intersection P=(4,8); tangent intercepts Q=(−4,0), R=(0,−8), so PQ=8√2 and QR=4√5.
Hexagon coordinates give H:x²/4−y²/12=1. Intersection P on AB has AP=3 and DP=7.
Lines from A intersect the ellipse iff |slope|≥1; the second intersection Q traces exactly the upper semicircle of radius 1, length π.
The tangent of slope −1 with positive y-intercept is y=−x+√5, with A=(√5,0), B=(0,√5); oriented area is 5.
Fold line is the perpendicular bisector of AF, hence PA=PF. Since P lies on OA inside the circle, OP+PF=OP+PA=OA=radius; thus the locus has fixed sum of distances to O and F and is an ellipse.
